# 2025 Tour Championship: The Restoration of Merit at East Lake
## 1\. Introduction
The **2025 Tour Championship** , disputed from August 21 to August 24, 2025, at the historic East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, Georgia, represents a seminal moment in the annals of the PGA TOUR. As the culminating event of the FedExCup Playoffs, the tournament has traditionally served as the season finale for the world's premier professional golf circuit. However, the 2025 edition was distinguished by two transformative developments that fundamentally altered the competitive landscape: a radical restructuring of the tournament format that erased the controversial "Starting Strokes" system, and the unveiling of a comprehensive architectural restoration of the venue by Andrew Green .

Tommy Fleetwood, the English standout who had long been burdened by the moniker of the "best player without a PGA TOUR victory," emerged triumphant. Fleetwood posted a four-round aggregate of 18-under-par (262) to secure his maiden title in the United States, capturing not only the Tour Championship trophy but also the FedExCup and its attendant $10 million first-place prize His victory, achieved on a level playing field without the artificial handicap of staggered starts, served as a validation of the Tour's decision to return to a pure 72-hole stroke play format.

The event featured the top 30 players from the FedExCup standings, who survived a grueling season-long qualification process and two preceding playoff events—the FedEx St. Jude Championship and the BMW Championship The total purse for the event was $40 million, the largest official purse for a single tournament in the 2025 season, underscoring the immense financial stakes involved .

This report provides an exhaustive record of the championship, analyzing the implications of the format overhaul, the agronomic and strategic shifts necessitated by the course restoration, the narrative arc of the competition, and the statistical realities that define the outcome.

## 2\. Evolution of the FedExCup Finale
### 2.1 The Abolition of "Starting Strokes"
For six years, spanning from the 2018-2019 season through 2024, the Tour Championship utilized a "Starting Strokes" (or staggered start) format. Under this system, the players at top the FedExCup standings entering East Lake began the tournament at 10-under-par, while the remaining 29 qualifiers were assigned starting scores ranging from 8-under down to even par based on their seeding. The objective was to simplify the viewing experience for casual fans: the player with the lowest score at the end of the week will win both the tournament and the FedExCup .

However, this format faced persistent criticism for manufacturing drama and potentially devaluing the performance of the week's actual lowest scorer. In a significant policy shift announced in May 2025, the PGA TOUR opted to eliminate starting strokes effective immediately for the 2025 Tour Championship . The 2025 event reverted to a traditional 72-hole stroke play competition where all 30 players began at even par (scratch) .

The implications of this reversion were profound. It shifted the competitive equity back toward immediate performance rather than season-long accumulation. Under the previous model, World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler—who entered the week as the points leader—would have enjoyed a two-stroke advantage over the field before striking a ball. In 2025, he was forced to tee off on Thursday level with the 30th-ranked qualifier, placing a premium on peak performance at the right moment .

### 2.2 Reactions and Competitive Philosophy
The return to a scratch start was widely debated within the golf ecosystem. Proponents argued that a season-ending championship should identify the best player of that specific week, akin to the Super Bowl or the World Series, where regular-season records determine seeding but not the starting score of the final match .

Critics, however, noted that the change diminished the value of the regular season. Scottie Scheffler, who had won five times in 2025 and dominated the points race, effectively saw his season-long lead erased at the first tee . The tension between rewarding consistency (the Regular Season) and volatility (the Playoffs) remained a central theme of the week. The "Shadow Leaderboard"—a statistical reconstruction of what the results would have been under the old format—became a key talking point post-tournament, highlighting the stark difference the rules change made to the ultimate champion (see Section 8: Statistical Analysis) .

### 2.3 Financial Restructuring and the Bonus Pool
The financial structure of the FedExCup was also recalibrated for 2025\. While the total bonus pool remained at a staggering $100 million, the distribution mechanism was altered to align with the new format.

* **Total Bonus Pool:** $100 million . 
* **Comcast Business TOUR TOP 10:** $20 million distributed to the top 10 finishers in the Regular Season (pre-playoffs) . 
* **Playoff Payouts:** Additional bonuses were awarded after the BMW Championship, leaving a $40 million purse specifically for the Tour Championship . 
* **Winner's Share:** The winner of the Tour Championship received $10 million. While this was a decrease from the $18 million and $25 million figures seen in the height of the "Starting Strokes" era, the $10 million was classified as official prize money, making it the largest official winner's check in PGA TOUR history .

This restructuring meant that the financial rewards were more evenly distributed throughout the season's checkpoints, but the $10 million Sunday payout remained the single most lucrative prize in the sport .

**Table 1: 2025 FedExCup Financial Structure Overview**

| Component | Allocation | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Total Bonus Pool** | $100,000,000 | Aggregate season-long bonus fund. |
| **Regular Season Bonus** | $20,000,000 | Distributed to top 10 in points post-Wyndham Championship. |
| **Playoff Deferrals** | $22,930,000 | Distributed to top 30 post-BMW Championship. |
| **Tour Championship Purse** | $40,000,000 | Immediate prize money for the East Lake field. |
| **Winner's Share** | $10,000,000 | Cash prize for the Tour Championship victor. |
| **Last Place Share** | $355,000 | Minimum payout for the 30th place finisher. |

Source: 5

## 3\. The Venue: East Lake Golf Club Restored
### 3.1 The Andrew Green Restoration
The 2025 Tour Championship marked the public debut of the newly restored East Lake Golf Club. The project was spearheaded by architect Andrew Green, who has gained renown for his sympathetic restorations of Golden Age courses like Inverness and Scioto. The objective was to peel back decades of alterations—most notably the extensive work done by Rees Jones in 1994—and return the course to the spirit of its original 1913 design by Donald Ross .

Green utilized aerial photography from 1949, previously unknown to historians, to guide the reshaping of the property. The restoration was not merely cosmetic; it fundamentally altered the strategic demands of the course. The "Rees Jones era" East Lake was characterized by narrow fairways, thick rough, and deep, flat-bottomed bunkers that demanded high aerial shots. The "Andrew Green era" East Lake, by contrast, reintroduced width, firm turf conditions, and complex ground game options .

### 3.2 Key Architectural Changes
The restoration touched every inch of the property, resulting in a course that played vastly different from previous years.

* **Green Complexes:** The putting surfaces were expanded significantly, often doubling in size. They were raised to create "turtleback" formations characteristic of Ross's work at Pinehurst No. 2\. The thick rough surrounding the greens was replaced with short-grass runoff areas. This change meant that missed greens resulted in balls rolling 30 or 40 yards away, challenging players to choose between putting, chipping, or using a hybrid for recovery . 
* **Bunkering:** The bunkers were reconstructed to be more strategic and less punitive in a one-dimensional sense. They were repositioned to cut into fairways, creating "zig-zag" corridors that forced players to challenge hazards to gain the optimal angle of approach. The sand lines were restored to a more rugged, natural aesthetic . 
* **The 14th Hole Conversion:** One of the most significant changes was the conversion of the 14th hole. In 2024, it played as a 580-yard Par 5, statistically the easiest hole on the course (4.33 scoring average). For 2025, Green shortened it to 530 yards but converted it into a Par 4\. This massive swing in par meant the hole transitioned from a guaranteed birdie opportunity to one of the most difficult Par 4s on the PGA TOUR, requiring a long iron or wood approach into a guarded green . 
* **The 15th Hole (Par 3):** The water hazard fronting the green was expanded, cutting further into the approach area. This increased the visual intimidation and the penalty for a mishit shot, particularly with the new wind patterns created by tree removal . 
* **The 1st Hole:** The opener was lengthened from 469 yards to 510 yards, creating a "baptism by fire." The fairway was narrowed, and the green reshaped to a shallower target with severe runoffs long, eliminating the "gentle handshake" start of previous years .

### 3.3 Agronomy and Conditions
The restoration also involved a complete agronomic overhaul. The turf was conditioned to play firm and fast, enhancing the effect of the new contours. The removal of trees improved airflow and turf health while opening up vistas across the property that had been obscured for decades. Players noted that the ball reacted differently on the ground, requiring a mental adjustment from "target golf" to a more cerebral, strategic approach .

**Table 2: East Lake Golf Club – Course Vital Statistics (2025)**

| Feature | Specification | Change from 2024 |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Par** | 70 | Unchanged (but composition differed) |
| **Yardage** | 7,440 yards | Lengthened/Adjusted |
| **Architect** | Donald Ross (1913) / Andrew Green (2025) | Restored from Rees Jones (1994) |
| **Grass Type** | Bermuda | New strains installed |
| **Key Modification** | Hole 14 | Converted from Par 5 to Par 4 (530 yards) |
| **Key Modification** | Greens | Expanded size, shaved runoffs added |

## 4\. Field Composition and Qualification
### 4.1 The Road to East Lake
Qualifying for the 2025 Tour Championship was statistically more difficult than in previous eras due to the reduction in field sizes throughout the FedExCup Playoffs. Only the top 70 players in the standings advanced to the first playoff event (FedEx St. Jude Championship), and only the top 50 advanced to the BMW Championship. From there, the field was whittled down to the final elite 30 for East Lake .

The points structure was reset entering the playoffs to increase volatility, ensuring that players had to perform in August to advance. Notable players who navigated this gauntlet included:

* **Scottie Scheffler:** The defending champion (2024) and season-long points leader. He entered East Lake with 7,456 points, a massive lead that was neutralized by the format change . 
* **Rory McIlroy:** A three-time FedExCup champion (2016, 2019, 2022\) making his eighth consecutive Tour Championship appearance, the longest active streak in the field. McIlroy entered ranked 2nd . 
* **Tommy Fleetwood:** The Englishman entered the week ranked 5th, following strong performances in the first two playoff events. He was seeking his first win in 164 starts . 
* **J.J. Spaun:** A surprise entrant at No. 3, having won the U.S. Open earlier in the season .

### 4.2 The Bubble and Withdrawals
The intensity of the "bubble" was highlighted by the drama surrounding the 30th spot. Sepp Straka, ranked high in the standings, withdrew from the BMW Championship due to a private family matter but retained enough points to qualify for East Lake in the 30th position, ultimately finishing the tournament in last place . 
Conversely, players like Xander Schauffele and Tony Finau saw their streaks of Tour Championship appearances snap after failing to advance past the earlier playoff stages . 
**Table 3: Top 5 Seeds Entering 2025 Tour Championship**

| 3 | J.J. Spaun | 3,493 | 0 |
| 4 | Justin Rose | 3,326 | 1 (2018) |
| 5 | Tommy Fleetwood | 2,923 | 0 |

## 5\. Tournament Narrative: Round by Round
### 5.1 Round 1: The Reset
Thursday, August 21, began with a palpable sense of a new era. For the first time in six years, the first group and the final group teed off with the same score: even par. The weather was typical for late August in Atlanta—hot and humid, with temperatures reaching 81°F and light winds .

The restored course immediately showed its teeth. The firm greens repelled approach shots that were merely "good," demanding "perfect" execution. Russell Henley, a University of Georgia alumnus comfortable on Bermuda grass, took immediate advantage of the clean slate. He fired a blistering 9-under-par 61, the low round of the tournament's early stages. His precision iron play allowed him to access hole locations that others could not hold .

Tommy Fleetwood opened with a solid 64 (-6), positioning himself three shots back. Conversely, World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler struggled to adapt to the loss of his starting strokes. He shot a 63 . The narrative quickly shifted from Scheffler's "coronation" to a dogfight.

### 5.2 Round 2: Fleetwood's Charge
Friday's second round proved pivotal. The course conditions remained consistent, but the pressure of the $40 million purse began to separate the field. Tommy Fleetwood produced the round of the day, a 7-under-par 63\. This propelled him to 13-under par for the tournament .

Fleetwood's ball-striking was clinical. He navigated the "zig-zag" fairways of the Andrew Green redesign with driving accuracy that led the field. He joined Russell Henley (who shot 66\) at the top of the leaderboard. Patrick Cantlay, the 2021 FedExCup champion, moved into contention with a 66, sitting poised to strike. Meanwhile, Scheffler's momentum stalled with a 69, dropping him off the lead pace—a deficit that would have been masked under the old format but was glaringly exposed in the new scratch scoring .

### 5.3 Round 3: Moving Day
Saturday, August 23, is traditionally "Moving Day," and the firming turf at East Lake made scoring increasingly difficult. The average score ballooned as the sub-air systems dried out the new greens.

Fleetwood displayed immense resilience, carding a 3-under 67\. While not as explosive as his Friday 63, it was a round defined by par saves from the new runoff areas, showcasing his short-game adaptability. Henley began to slide, shooting a 69, while Cantlay matched Fleetwood's intensity with a 64, setting up a final-round showdown .

Heading into Sunday, the leaderboard was tight:

* Fleetwood: \-16 
* Henley: \-14 
* Cantlay: \-14 
* Scheffler: \-12

### 5.4 Round 4: The Coronation
Sunday, August 24, provided a dramatic conclusion to the season. With $10 million on the line, the tension was evident in the opening holes.

Fleetwood, seeking his first win, opened steadily. A key moment occurred on the par-4 7th hole. After driving into one of the newly renovated fairway bunkers, Fleetwood struck a magnificent approach shot from the sand to 12 feet and converted the birdie. This moved him to 18-under and seemed to signal a runaway victory .

However, the back nine at East Lake is famous for volatility. Fleetwood stumbled at the 10th hole, making bogey after missing a par putt on the high side. Simultaneously, Patrick Cantlay birdied the 10th, creating a two-shot swing that cut Fleetwood's lead to a single stroke. The tournament was suddenly in the balance .

Fleetwood responded with the poise of a veteran. He parred the difficult 14th (the new long Par 4\) and navigated the island-green 15th safely. As his challengers faltered—Cantlay bogeyed late to shoot 71—Fleetwood kept his card clean. Russell Henley fought back with a 69 to tie Cantlay for second.

The shot of the day, however, belonged to Corey Conners. Playing well ahead of the leaders, the Canadian fired a spectacular 8-under 62, the lowest round of the weekend, vaulting him into a tie for 4th place. This performance perfectly illustrated the benefits of the new format: Conners' Sunday brilliance was rewarded with a massive payday ($2.6 million), whereas under the staggered start, he would likely have been too far back to matter .

Fleetwood closed with a 2-under 68, finishing at 18-under-par (262). He walked up the 18th fairway to an ovation, tapping in for par to secure a three-shot victory over Henley and Cantlay .

## 6\. Statistical Analysis and The "Shadow Leaderboard"
### 6.1 Performance Metrics
The statistics from the week underscored the difficulty of the Andrew Green restoration. While the leaders went low, the scoring average for the field was higher than in previous years.

* **Dispersion:** The gap between the winner (-18) and the last-place finisher (Sepp Straka at \+7) was 25 strokes. This massive dispersion highlights the penal nature of the course for those who were slightly off-form . 
* **Hole Difficulty:** The newly converted 14th hole played as the most difficult on the course, a complete reversal from its status as the easiest hole in 2024\. The 18th hole remained a birdie opportunity (Par 5), playing to a 4.38 average, allowing for late drama .

### 6.2 The "Shadow Leaderboard" Controversy
The 2025 Tour Championship provides a unique case study in tournament formatting. Because the "Starting Strokes" format was used so recently, analysts immediately calculated what the outcome *would* have been had the old rules applied. This hypothetical ranking, known as the "Shadow Leaderboard," revealed that the format change directly altered the history of the FedExCup.

Under the old format:

* **Scottie Scheffler** would have started at \-10. 
* **Tommy Fleetwood** (Ranked 5th) would have started at \-5.

If we add these starting strokes to their actual gross scores:

* **Scheffler:** \-14 (Gross) \+ (-10 Start) \= **\-24 Total** 
* **Fleetwood:** \-18 (Gross) \+ (-5 Start) \= **\-23 Total**

**Conclusion:** Under the 2024 rules, Scottie Scheffler would have won the FedExCup by one stroke. Under the 2025 rules, Tommy Fleetwood won by four strokes (over Scheffler). This single data point validates the arguments of both sides: Scheffler was the "best season-long player," but Fleetwood was undeniably the "best player this week." The Tour's decision to prioritize the latter cost Scheffler $7.5 million (the difference between 1st and T4 money) and a major title .

| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |

## 7\. Financial Breakdown
The $40 million purse at the 2025 Tour Championship was distributed with a heavy weighting toward the champion. The payout structure ensured that every player in the field received substantial compensation, reflecting the achievement of qualifying for the season finale.

* **Winner:** $10,000,000 (25% of purse) 
* **Runner-Up:** $4,352,500 (approx. 10.8% of purse) 
* **Top 10:** All top 10 finishers earned over $700,000. 
* **Last Place:** Sepp Straka earned $355,000 for finishing 30th .

This payout structure is significant because it rewards "showing up" to a high degree but places a massive premium on winning. The difference between 1st place ($10M) and T2 ($4.35M) was over $5.6 million for a single stroke (or in this case, three strokes).

## 8\. Legacy and Implications
### 8.1 Fleetwood's Breakthrough
Tommy Fleetwood's victory reshaped the narrative of his career. Having amassed over $20 million in career earnings prior to this event without a win on the PGA TOUR, he was often cited as a statistical anomaly. His victory at East Lake, against the strongest field of the year and under the pressure of the largest purse in history, firmly established his elite status. In his post-round interview, an emotional Fleetwood remarked on the resilience required to overcome years of "near misses," citing the victory as proof that persistence pays off .

### 8.2 The Future of the Format
The 2025 Tour Championship will likely serve as the benchmark for future FedExCup formats. The excitement generated by the "scratch" leaderboard, where multiple players (Fleetwood, Henley, Cantlay) had a legitimate chance to win on Sunday, was contrasted favorably against the "coronations" of the Starting Strokes era. The fan response, and the Tour's "Fan Forward" initiative, suggests that this format is likely to remain in place for the foreseeable future .

### 8.3 East Lake's New Identity
The Andrew Green restoration was universally praised for revitalizing a classic venue. East Lake is no longer defined merely by its difficulty or its history with Bobby Jones, but by its architectural merit. The course now demands a complete examination of a golfer's skill set—mental, strategic, and physical. As the permanent home of the Tour Championship, the restored East Lake provides a fittingly stern and sophisticated stage for the PGA TOUR's ultimate prize .

In conclusion, the 2025 Tour Championship was a triumph of reinvention. By looking backward—restoring the course to its 1913 roots and the format to its stroke-play traditions—the PGA TOUR successfully pushed the FedExCup forward into a new era of competitive integrity and excitement.

## 9\. Player Biographies and Contextual Performance
### 9.1 Tommy Fleetwood (Winner)
Born in Southport, England, Fleetwood's journey to the 2025 Tour Championship title was one of the most compelling narratives in modern golf. Known for his distinctive long hair and supreme ball-striking, Fleetwood had become a folk hero in Europe (winning the Race to Dubai) but a tragic figure in the US, often finishing second in majors (US Open at Shinnecock, Open Championship at Portrush).

* **Performance Context:** Fleetwood entered the week in form, having finished T5 in the preceding playoff events. His victory was built on the foundation of his iron play, which neutralized the firm runoff areas of the new East Lake. 
* **Key Moment:** The bunker shot on No. 7 in the final round will be replayed as the shot that finally broke the dam .

### 9.2 Scottie Scheffler (T4)
The 2024 FedExCup Champion arrived in Atlanta as the undisputed best player in the world. His season included a second Green Jacket at the Masters and a Players Championship title.

* **The Format Victim:** Scheffler became the face of the format change debate. His reaction to the loss—gracious but clearly disappointed—will be a footnote in the history of the 2025 season. Despite finishing T4, his season earnings of over $50 million (including bonuses) remains a record .

### 9.3 Rory McIlroy (T23)
The three-time champion never found his footing on the restored course. McIlroy, who thrived on the "high aerial" demands of the old East Lake, struggled to adapt to the ground game required by Andrew Green's runoffs. He finished T23, earning $395,000, a quiet end to a tumultuous season .

The bunkers at East Lake Golf Club were repositioned to cut into fairways, creating "zig-zag" corridors that forced players to challenge hazards to gain the optimal angle of approach.
The sand lines at East Lake Golf Club were restored to a more rugged, natural aesthetic.
One of the most significant changes at East Lake Golf Club was the conversion of the 14th hole.
In 2024, the 14th hole at East Lake Golf Club played as a 580-yard Par 5.
In 2024, the 14th hole at East Lake Golf Club was statistically the easiest hole on the course with a 4.33 scoring average.
For 2025, Andrew Green shortened the 14th hole to 530 yards and converted it into a Par 4.
The 14th hole transitioned from a guaranteed birdie opportunity to one of the most difficult Par 4s on the PGA TOUR, requiring a long iron or wood approach into a guarded green.
The water hazard fronting the green on the 15th hole (Par 3) at East Lake Golf Club was expanded, cutting further into the approach area.
The expansion of the water hazard on the 15th hole increased visual intimidation and the penalty for a mishit shot, particularly with new wind patterns created by tree removal.
The 1st hole at East Lake Golf Club was lengthened from 469 yards to 510 yards.
The fairway on the 1st hole at East Lake Golf Club was narrowed.
The green on the 1st hole at East Lake Golf Club was reshaped to a shallower target with severe runoffs long.
The restoration of East Lake Golf Club involved a complete agronomic overhaul.
The turf at East Lake Golf Club was conditioned to play firm and fast, enhancing the effect of the new contours.
The removal of trees at East Lake Golf Club improved airflow and turf health while opening up vistas across the property that had been obscured for decades.
Players noted that the ball reacted differently on the ground at East Lake Golf Club, requiring a mental adjustment from "target golf" to a more cerebral, strategic approach.
The par for East Lake Golf Club in 2025 was 70, which was unchanged from 2024, but its composition differed.
The yardage for East Lake Golf Club in 2025 was 7,440 yards, which was lengthened/adjusted from 2024.
The architect of East Lake Golf Club was Donald Ross (1913), and it was restored by Andrew Green (2025) from Rees Jones (1994).
The grass type at East Lake Golf Club is Bermuda, with new strains installed.
A key modification at East Lake Golf Club was the conversion of Hole 14 from Par 5 to Par 4 (530 yards).
A key modification at East Lake Golf Club was the expansion of greens and the addition of shaved runoffs.
Qualifying for the 2025 Tour Championship was statistically more difficult than in previous eras due to the reduction in field sizes throughout the FedExCup Playoffs.
Only the top 70 players in the standings advanced to the first playoff event (FedEx St. Jude Championship).
Only the top 50 players advanced to the BMW Championship.
From the BMW Championship, the field was whittled down to the final elite 30 for East Lake.
The points structure was reset entering the playoffs to increase volatility, ensuring that players had to perform in August to advance.
Scottie Scheffler, the defending champion (2024) and season-long points leader, entered East Lake with 7,456 points.
Scottie Scheffler's massive lead was neutralized by the format change.
Rory McIlroy is a three-time FedExCup champion (2016, 2019, 2022).
Rory McIlroy made his eighth consecutive Tour Championship appearance, which is the longest active streak in the field.
Rory McIlroy entered the 2025 Tour Championship ranked 2nd.
Tommy Fleetwood entered the week ranked 5th, following strong performances in the first two playoff events.
Tommy Fleetwood was seeking his first win in 164 starts.
J.J. Spaun was a surprise entrant at No. 3, having won the U.S. Open earlier in the season.
Sepp Straka withdrew from the BMW Championship due to a private family matter but retained enough points to qualify for East Lake in the 30th position.
Sepp Straka ultimately finished the tournament in last place.
Players like Xander Schauffele and Tony Finau saw their streaks of Tour Championship appearances snap after failing to advance past the earlier playoff stages.
Scottie Scheffler was ranked 1st with 7,456 points entering the 2025 Tour Championship.
Scottie Scheffler had 1 previous Tour Championship win (2024).
Rory McIlroy was ranked 2nd with 3,687 points entering the 2025 Tour Championship.
Rory McIlroy had 3 previous Tour Championship wins (2016, 2019, 2022).
J.J. Spaun was ranked 3rd with 3,493 points entering the 2025 Tour Championship.
J.J. Spaun had 0 previous Tour Championship wins.
Justin Rose was ranked 4th with 3,326 points entering the 2025 Tour Championship.
Justin Rose had 1 previous Tour Championship win (2018).
Tommy Fleetwood was ranked 5th with 2,923 points entering the 2025 Tour Championship.
Tommy Fleetwood had 0 previous Tour Championship wins.
Thursday, August 21, began with a palpable sense of a new era at the 2025 Tour Championship.
For the first time in six years, the first group and the final group teed off with the same score: even par.
The weather on Thursday, August 21, was typical for late August in Atlanta—hot and humid, with temperatures reaching 81°F and light winds.
The restored course immediately showed its teeth, with firm greens repelling approach shots that were merely "good," demanding "perfect" execution.
Russell Henley, a University of Georgia alumnus comfortable on Bermuda grass, fired a blistering 9-under-par 61.
Russell Henley's 9-under-par 61 was the low round of the tournament's early stages.
Russell Henley's precision iron play allowed him to access hole locations that others could not hold.
Tommy Fleetwood opened with a solid 64 (-6), positioning himself three shots back.
World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler struggled to adapt to the loss of his starting strokes and shot a 63.
Friday's second round proved pivotal at the 2025 Tour Championship.
The course conditions remained consistent on Friday, but the pressure of the $40 million purse began to separate the field.
Tommy Fleetwood produced the round of the day, a 7-under-par 63.
Tommy Fleetwood's 7-under-par 63 propelled him to 13-under par for the tournament.
Tommy Fleetwood's ball-striking was clinical, and he navigated the "zig-zag" fairways of the Andrew Green redesign with driving accuracy that led the field.
Tommy Fleetwood joined Russell Henley (who shot 66) at the top of the leaderboard.
Patrick Cantlay, the 2021 FedExCup champion, moved into contention with a 66.
Scottie Scheffler's momentum stalled with a 69, dropping him off the lead pace.
Saturday, August 23, is traditionally "Moving Day" in golf.
The firming turf at East Lake made scoring increasingly difficult on Saturday.
The average score ballooned on Saturday as the sub-air systems dried out the new greens.
Tommy Fleetwood displayed immense resilience, carding a 3-under 67.
Tommy Fleetwood's round of 67 was defined by par saves from the new runoff areas, showcasing his short-game adaptability.
Russell Henley began to slide, shooting a 69.
Patrick Cantlay matched Fleetwood's intensity with a 64, setting up a final-round showdown.
Heading into Sunday, Fleetwood was at -16.
Heading into Sunday, Henley was at -14.
Heading into Sunday, Cantlay was at -14.
Heading into Sunday, Scheffler was at -12.
Sunday, August 24, provided a dramatic conclusion to the season.
Fleetwood opened steadily on Sunday, seeking his first win.
A key moment occurred on the par-4 7th hole when Fleetwood struck a magnificent approach shot from a newly renovated fairway bunker to 12 feet and converted the birdie.
Fleetwood's birdie on the 7th hole moved him to 18-under.
Fleetwood stumbled at the 10th hole, making bogey after missing a par putt on the high side.
Patrick Cantlay birdied the 10th, creating a two-shot swing that cut Fleetwood's lead to a single stroke.
Fleetwood responded with the poise of a veteran, parring the difficult 14th (the new long Par 4) and navigating the island-green 15th safely.
Cantlay bogeyed late to shoot 71.
Russell Henley fought back with a 69 to tie Cantlay for second.
The shot of the day belonged to Corey Conners.
Corey Conners fired a spectacular 8-under 62, the lowest round of the weekend, vaulting him into a tie for 4th place.
Conners' Sunday brilliance was rewarded with a massive payday ($2.6 million).
Fleetwood closed with a 2-under 68, finishing at 18-under-par (262).
Tommy Fleetwood secured a three-shot victory over Henley and Cantlay.
Tommy Fleetwood (ENG) finished 1st with a total score of 262 (-18) and earnings of $10,000,000.
Russell Henley (USA) finished T2 with a total score of 265 (-15) and earnings of $4,352,500.
Patrick Cantlay (USA) finished T2 with a total score of 265 (-15) and earnings of $4,352,500.
Corey Conners (CAN) finished T4 with a total score of 266 (-14) and earnings of $2,616,667.
Scottie Scheffler (USA) finished T4 with a total score of 266 (-14) and earnings of $2,616,667.
Cameron Young (USA) finished T4 with a total score of 266 (-14) and earnings of $2,616,667.
Justin Thomas (USA) finished T7 with a total score of 267 (-13) and earnings of $1,121,667.
Sam Burns (USA) finished T7 with a total score of 267 (-13) and earnings of $1,121,667.
Keegan Bradley (USA) finished T7 with a total score of 267 (-13) and earnings of $1,121,667.
Chris Gotterup (USA) finished T10 with a total score of 268 (-12) and earnings of $715,000.
Ben Griffin (USA) finished T10 with a total score of 268 (-12) and earnings of $715,000.
The statistics from the week underscored the difficulty of the Andrew Green restoration.
The scoring average for the field was higher than in previous years.
The gap between the winner (-18) and the last-place finisher (Sepp Straka at +7) was 25 strokes.
The massive dispersion highlights the penal nature of the course for those who were slightly off-form.
The newly converted 14th hole played as the most difficult on the course, a complete reversal from its status as the easiest hole in 2024.
The 18th hole remained a birdie opportunity (Par 5), playing to a 4.38 average.
The 2025 Tour Championship provides a unique case study in tournament formatting.
Because the "Starting Strokes" format was used so recently, analysts immediately calculated what the outcome would have been had the old rules applied.
The hypothetical ranking, known as the "Shadow Leaderboard," revealed that the format change directly altered the history of the FedExCup.
Under the old format, Scottie Scheffler would have started at -10.
Under the old format, Tommy Fleetwood (Ranked 5th) would have started at -5.
If starting strokes were added to their actual gross scores, Scheffler's simulated total would be -24.
If starting strokes were added to their actual gross scores, Fleetwood's simulated total would be -23.
Under the 2024 rules, Scottie Scheffler would have won the FedExCup by one stroke.
Under the 2025 rules, Tommy Fleetwood won by four strokes (over Scheffler).
The Tour's decision to prioritize the best player of the week cost Scheffler $7.5 million (the difference between 1st and T4 money) and a major title.
Tommy Fleetwood's actual gross score was -18.
Tommy Fleetwood's simulated starting strokes were -5.
Tommy Fleetwood's simulated total score was -23.
Tommy Fleetwood won in '25 but would have lost in the '24 Format.
Scottie Scheffler's actual gross score was -14.
Scottie Scheffler's simulated starting strokes were -10.
Scottie Scheffler's simulated total score was -24.
Scottie Scheffler lost in '25 but would have won in the '24 Format.
Russell Henley's actual gross score was -15.
Russell Henley's simulated starting strokes were -4.
Russell Henley's simulated total score was -19.
Russell Henley had no change in his Top 5 position.
Patrick Cantlay's actual gross score was -15.
Patrick Cantlay's simulated starting strokes were -2.
Patrick Cantlay's simulated total score was -17.
Patrick Cantlay had no change in his Top 5 position.
The $40 million purse at the 2025 Tour Championship was distributed with a heavy weighting toward the champion.
The payout structure ensured that every player in the field received substantial compensation, reflecting the achievement of qualifying for the season finale.
The winner of the 2025 Tour Championship received $10,000,000 (25% of the purse).
The runner-up of the 2025 Tour Championship received $4,352,500 (approximately 10.8% of the purse).
All top 10 finishers at the 2025 Tour Championship earned over $700,000.
Sepp Straka earned $355,000 for finishing 30th at the 2025 Tour Championship.
The payout structure rewards "showing up" to a high degree but places a massive premium on winning.
The difference between 1st place ($10M) and T2 ($4.35M) was over $5.6 million for a single stroke (or in this case, three strokes).
Tommy Fleetwood earned $10,000,000 at the 2025 Tour Championship.
Russell Henley earned $4,352,500 at the 2025 Tour Championship.
Patrick Cantlay earned $4,352,500 at the 2025 Tour Championship.
Corey Conners earned $2,616,667 at the 2025 Tour Championship.
Viktor Hovland earned $660,000 at the 2025 Tour Championship.
Brian Harman earned $570,000 at the 2025 Tour Championship.
Harry Hall earned $482,500 at the 2025 Tour Championship.
Collin Morikawa earned $452,500 at the 2025 Tour Championship.
Hideki Matsuyama earned $360,000 at the 2025 Tour Championship.
Sepp Straka earned $355,000 at the 2025 Tour Championship.
Tommy Fleetwood's victory reshaped the narrative of his career.
Tommy Fleetwood had amassed over $20 million in career earnings prior to this event without a win on the PGA TOUR.
Tommy Fleetwood's victory at East Lake, against the strongest field of the year and under the pressure of the largest purse in history, firmly established his elite status.
Tommy Fleetwood remarked on the resilience required to overcome years of "near misses" in his post-round interview.
Tommy Fleetwood cited the victory as proof that persistence pays off.
The 2025 Tour Championship will likely serve as the benchmark for future FedExCup formats.

The excitement generated by the "scratch" leaderboard, where multiple players (Fleetwood, Henley, Cantlay) had a legitimate chance to win on Sunday, was contrasted favorably against the "coronations" of the Starting Strokes era.
The fan response and the Tour's "Fan Forward" initiative suggest that this format is likely to remain in place for the foreseeable future.
The Andrew Green restoration was universally praised for revitalizing a classic venue.
East Lake is no longer defined merely by its difficulty or its history with Bobby Jones, but by its architectural merit.
The restored East Lake course now demands a complete examination of a golfer's skill set—mental, strategic, and physical.
As the permanent home of the Tour Championship, the restored East Lake provides a fittingly stern and sophisticated stage for the PGA TOUR's ultimate prize.
Tommy Fleetwood's journey to the 2025 Tour Championship title was one of the most compelling narratives in modern golf.
Tommy Fleetwood is known for his distinctive long hair and supreme ball-striking.
Tommy Fleetwood had become a folk hero in Europe (winning the Race to Dubai) but a tragic figure in the US, often finishing second in majors (US Open at Shinnecock, Open Championship at Portrush).
Tommy Fleetwood entered the week in form, having finished T5 in the preceding playoff events.
Tommy Fleetwood's victory was built on the foundation of his iron play, which neutralized the firm runoff areas of the new East Lake.
The bunker shot on No. 7 in the final round will be replayed as the shot that finally broke the dam for Tommy Fleetwood.
Scottie Scheffler, the 2024 FedExCup Champion, arrived in Atlanta as the undisputed best player in the world.
Scottie Scheffler's season included a second Green Jacket at the Masters and a Players Championship title.
Scottie Scheffler became the face of the format change debate.
Scottie Scheffler's reaction to the loss—gracious but clearly disappointed—will be a footnote in the history of the 2025 season.
Despite finishing T4, Scottie Scheffler's season earnings of over $50 million (including bonuses) remains a record.
Rory McIlroy, a three-time champion, never found his footing on the restored course.
Rory McIlroy struggled to adapt to the ground game required by Andrew Green's runoffs, despite thriving on the "high aerial" demands of the old East Lake.
Rory McIlroy finished T23, earning $395,000, which was a quiet end to a tumultuous season.

2.content:
The PGA TOUR season reaches its climax at East Lake Golf Club, where the FedExCup’s top 30 will battle for one of golf’s most prestigious prizes.

![Image 1: Scottie Scheffler](https://img.olympics.com/images/image/private/t_s_16_9_g_auto/t_s_w960/f_auto/primary/afstrvkeppea4gj3kbxt)

Picture by 2024 Mike Mulholland

By William Imbo

 18 August 2025 12:55 GMT+0 3 min read

The finale of the PGA TOUR FedExCup Playoffs has arrived.

The 2025 TOUR Championship takes place from Thursday to Sunday (21–24 August) at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta, Georgia, where the top 30 men’s [golfers](https://www.olympics.com/en/sports/golf/) in the FedExCup standings will compete for the FedExCup.

Below is everything you need to know about the season-ending showdown, including the full schedule, featured players, and how to watch the action live.

*   [Japan's Iwai Akie, Chisato become first twins to win in LPGA history](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/golf-women-japan-iwai-akie-chisato-twins)

2025 PGA TOUR Championship at a glance
--------------------------------------

*   **Dates**: 21-24 August 2025
*   **Venue**: East Lake Golf Club, Atlanta, Georgia
*   **Format**: Stroke play, 72 holes, FedExCup staggered start scoring
*   **Field**: Top 30 in FedExCup standings
*   **Purse**: $75 million FedExCup bonus pool
*   **Defending champion**: Scottie Scheffler
*   **Season impact**: Winner claims the FedExCup

Golfers to watch
----------------

[**Scottie Scheffler**](https://www.olympics.com/en/athletes/scottie-scheffler)'s new nickname may as well be _Thanos_, because like the “Mad Titan,” he is inevitable. On Sunday, 17 August, he added another triumph to his extraordinary 2025 season at the **BMW Championship**, staging a breathtaking comeback to erase a four-shot deficit to Robert MacIntyre and ultimately win by two strokes—capped by a jaw-dropping chip-in on the 17th hole. It’s Scheffler’s **fifth win of the 2025 PGA Tour season**, following victories at **The Open Championship, Memorial Tournament, PGA Championship, and the CJ CUP**. With virtually no weaknesses in his game and riding a red-hot winning streak, Scheffler enters East Lake as the man to beat once again.

[**Rory McIlroy**](https://www.olympics.com/en/athletes/rory-mcilroy) has had a remarkable 2025 season, highlighted by his victory at The Masters, completing his career Grand Slam. He also secured wins at the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am and The Players Championship. His consistent performances have kept him near the top of the FedExCup standings, where he ranks second behind Scheffler.

**[Tommy Fleetwood](https://www.olympics.com/en/athletes/tommy-fleetwood)** is another big name to watch. The Englishman fired a final-round 67 to finish tied for fourth at the BMW Championship and currently sits fifth in the FedExCup standings. The [**Paris 2024**](https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-2024) silver medallist’s 2025 season has been marked by near-misses, including a runner-up finish at the Travelers Championship and a tie for third at the FedEx St. Jude Championship. With **30 top-five finishes on the PGA Tour without a win**, the Tour Championship would be the perfect stage for Fleetwood to finally break that unwanted streak.

2025 TOUR Championship full schedule: Dates, start times, and tee times
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

Official practice rounds at East Lake Golf Club begin on Monday, 18 August, and continue through Wednesday, 20 August.

All times are local (EDT – Eastern Daylight Time).

*   **Thursday, 21 August – Round 1:** 11:20 a.m.–2:00 p.m.

*   **Friday, 22 August – Round 2:** 11:20 a.m.–2:00 p.m.

*   **Saturday, 23 August – Round 3:** 12:10 p.m.–2:55 p.m.

*   **Sunday, 24 August – Round 4:** 11:20 a.m.–2:00 p.m.

2025 TOUR Championship: How to watch live
-----------------------------------------

Coverage of the TOUR Championship will be available to fans in more than 200 countries through television and digital broadcast partners. You can also watch the event live on [Olympics.com](https://www.olympics.com/en/sport-events/2025-pga-golf-tour-championship-atlanta)!

*   **United States:** Golf Channel and NBC provide live television coverage across all four days, with streaming available via Peacock.

*   **United Kingdom:** Sky Sports Golf will broadcast the tournament, with live radio commentary available on talkSPORT 2.

The tournament is televised worldwide through more than 30 official partners. Check local listings or visit the TOUR Championship’s official broadcast partner directory for regional coverage information.

[![Image 8: John L. Scott Real Estate office at 900 West Main Street in Centralia, Washington](https://www.elisportsnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/johnlscottbannerad.png)](https://centraliaoffice.johnlscott.com/)

[![Image 9: The image contains the Tyler Rental logo, the address 153 N Hamilton Rd, Chehalis, WA, the phone number (360) 748-3440, and a fleet of heavy equipment](https://www.elisportsnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/TYLER-RENTAL-BANNER.png)](https://www.tylerrental.net/)

[![Image 10: NAPA Auto Parts and Wilson Parts Corporation logo](https://www.elisportsnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wilson-Parts-Corporation.png)](https://www.wilsonnapa.com/)

5/29/25

The PGA Tour announced on Tuesday that the format for the TOUR Championship would revert to its original format, with no starting strokes. Recently, the format was a starting strokes format, where, depending on where players were in the FedEx Cup Standings, that would determine how many strokes under par players would start at for the TOUR Championship. The FedEx Cup has recently been decided at the TOUR Championship, with whoever wins the season finale wins the FedEx Cup.

The PGA Tour has decided to eliminate the starting strokes, and everyone starts at even par, like a normal golf tournament. Last year, Scottie Scheffler had the benefit of the starting strokes to win the FedEx Cup, despite Collin Morikawa having the lowest gross score for the week.

The fans weren’t too thrilled about the changes to the playoffs, where the winner of the TOUR Championship wins the FedEx Cup. Fans were even less thrilled about the starting strokes experiment for the last six years.

It’s also fascinating that the change is happening in the middle of the season. Not too often does a league or sport change the way its season-long championship is won, during that season. While there’s still not a perfect playoff format for individual sports, it’s a step in the right direction.

[![Image 11: NAPA Auto Parts and Wilson Parts Corporation logo](https://www.elisportsnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Wilson-Parts-Corporation.png)](https://www.wilsonnapa.com/)

[![Image 12](https://www.elisportsnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/CC-Chamber-banner.png)](http://chamberway.com/)

[![Image 13: The logo for Emerald Downs Racetrack & Casino features a mountain range with the outline of a horse's head and tail above it](https://www.elisportsnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/emeraldbanner.jpg)](https://emeralddowns.com/)

[![Image 14: We support students! in navy blue, the Centralia College Foundation logo, the phone number 360-623-8942, and the email foundation.centralia.edu](https://www.elisportsnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/08/CCF-Eli-Sports-Ads_banner.jpg)](http://www.centralia.edu/)

[![Image 15: John L. Scott Real Estate office at 900 West Main Street in Centralia, Washington](https://www.elisportsnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/johnlscottbannerad.png)](https://centraliaoffice.johnlscott.com/)

[![Image 16: The image contains the Tyler Rental logo, the address 153 N Hamilton Rd, Chehalis, WA, the phone number (360) 748-3440, and a fleet of heavy equipment](https://www.elisportsnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/TYLER-RENTAL-BANNER.png)](https://www.tylerrental.net/)

[![Image 17: Proactive Physical Therapy provides physical therapy and performance training](https://www.elisportsnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/proactive-banner.jpg)](https://www.proactivesportsmed.com/physical-therapy)

[![Image 18: The thorbeckes logo in black with a gray trapezoid to the left and three gray lines to the right](https://www.elisportsnetwork.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/thorbeckes728_90.png)](http://thorbeckes.com/)

Individual sports are unique from team sports, where winning the season-long championship doesn’t typically equate to winning a crown-jewel event. People don’t recite that Tiger Woods has won the FedEx Cup twice. They remember he’s won 15 major championships. Hélio Castroneves never won IndyCar’s season-long championship, but he’s won the Indianapolis 500 four times, and IndyCar fans remember that. Dale Earnhardt won seven Winston Cup Championships (NASCAR), but the big knock on The Intimidator was that he didn’t win the Daytona 500 until 1998 in his 20th attempt.

The list goes on, but the point is, not every sport needs to have an extravagant season-long championship. Golf has four to six weekends out of the year, depending on the year, where it’s one of, if not the main, focus of the sports world. That’s not bad, compared to some team sports. Most importantly, golf capitalizes on the schedule not having its peak events NFL’d. The PGA Tour schedule avoids the NFL season for the most part. The majors have no obstruction from the NFL schedule, whether it’s games, the draft, free agency, etc.

Men’s professional golf is in a tricky spot. Golf YouTuber videos garner more views than some professional golf tournaments. There are two tours that at first hated each other, but now are trying to negotiate a deal, and no one knows what the status is on these negotiations. There also isn’t another Tiger Woods that will burst onto the scene and bring the game the popularity it saw in the 2000s. So yes, men’s professional golf has to get creative to draw in the most viewers and fans. Attempting to manufacture drama isn’t how to do it.

However, at least they are beginning to listen to their most ardent fans. Next on the agenda, get rid of those obnoxious big block letter hats.

You deserve an explanation, so please don't skip this 1-minute read. It's Sunday, December 21. Our fundraiser will soon be over, but we're short of our goal. If you've lost count of how many times you've visited Wikipedia this year, we hope that means it's given you at least $2.75 of knowledge. If everyone who finds Wikipedia useful gave $2.75, we'd hit our goal in a few hours.

It's been 25 years and Wikipedia is still free. It's still created by people, not machines, and we don't run ads or put up paywalls because we're not here to make a profit off your attention. In other words, it's still the internet we were promised.

Less than 2% of our readers donate, so if you have given in the past and Wikipedia still provides you with $2.75 worth of knowledge, donate today. If you are undecided, remember any contribution helps.

25 years of the internet at its **best**

How would you like to be reminded?

Whether you give now or later, any contribution helps. We can send you an email or text message reminder to join the 2% of readers who donate.

Thank you for donating recently!

Your support means the world to us. We'll hide banners in this browser for the rest of our campaign.

Want to show off your support? **Donors get 20% off Wikipedia Store merchandise automatically applied at checkout.** Click the button below to shop hats, tees, and more!

Other ways to give

[More ways to give](https://wikimediafoundation.org/give/#ways-to-give)
Where your donation goes

Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://annual.wikimedia.org/) for more information about our financial health.

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

34% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

11% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

The **2025 PGA Tour** was the 110th season of the [PGA Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGA_Tour "PGA Tour"), the main [professional golf tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_golf_tour "Professional golf tour") in the United States. It was also the 57th season since separating from the [PGA of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGA_of_America "PGA of America"), and the 19th edition of the [FedEx Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FedEx_Cup "FedEx Cup").

In May 2025, the PGA Tour announced updates to the format of the season-ending [Tour Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_Championship "Tour Championship"). Beginning this year, starting strokes, first introduced for the [2018–19 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_PGA_Tour "2018–19 PGA Tour"), will be eliminated, with the tournament now being played as a regular 72-hole stroke-play event, with all players starting the tournament at even par.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_PGA_Tour#cite_note-Changes2025-1)

The eligibility categories also changed. The top 70 would be exempt for the FedEx Cup, with those up to 100th retaining full status (down from 125th), and conditional up to 125th (down from 150th).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_PGA_Tour#cite_note-Changes2025-1)

The top 50 points scorers after FedEx St. Jude Championship qualify for the [BMW Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_Championship_(PGA_Tour) "BMW Championship (PGA Tour)").
7.   **[^](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_PGA_Tour#cite_ref-Champ_15-0 "Jump up")**The top 30 point scorers after the [BMW Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BMW_Championship_(PGA_Tour) "BMW Championship (PGA Tour)") qualify for the [Tour Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tour_Championship "Tour Championship"). The player who scored the lowest in the Tour Championship won the [FedEx Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FedEx_Cup "FedEx Cup").

Tour Championship payout distribution 2025: Purse, winner's prize money
=======================================================================

How much prize money is on the line at the season-ending Tour Championship?

By[Josh Chandler](https://progolfnow.com/author/jchandler)|Aug 24, 2025

[](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=531030426978426&display=popup&href=https:%2F%2Fprogolfnow.com%2Ftour-championship-payout-distribution-2025-purse-winners-prize-money)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Tour%20Championship%20payout%20distribution%202025:%20Purse%2C%20winner%27s%20prize%20money&url=https:%2F%2Fprogolfnow.com%2Ftour-championship-payout-distribution-2025-purse-winners-prize-money)[](http://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https:%2F%2Fprogolfnow.com%2Ftour-championship-payout-distribution-2025-purse-winners-prize-money&title=Tour%20Championship%20payout%20distribution%202025:%20Purse%2C%20winner%27s%20prize%20money)

![Image 6: A view of the 18th hole at East Lake Golf Club, home of the Tour Championship](https://images2.minutemediacdn.com/image/upload/c_crop,x_0,y_565,w_5526,h_3108/c_fill,w_720,ar_16:9,f_auto,q_auto,g_auto/images/GettyImages/mmsport/120/01k3cyf38a0r0d85nd1z.jpg)

A view of the 18th hole at East Lake Golf Club, home of the Tour Championship | Jared C. Tilton/GettyImages

[](https://www.facebook.com/dialog/share?app_id=531030426978426&display=popup&href=https:%2F%2Fprogolfnow.com%2Ftour-championship-payout-distribution-2025-purse-winners-prize-money)[](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Tour%20Championship%20payout%20distribution%202025:%20Purse%2C%20winner%27s%20prize%20money&url=https:%2F%2Fprogolfnow.com%2Ftour-championship-payout-distribution-2025-purse-winners-prize-money)[](http://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https:%2F%2Fprogolfnow.com%2Ftour-championship-payout-distribution-2025-purse-winners-prize-money&title=Tour%20Championship%20payout%20distribution%202025:%20Purse%2C%20winner%27s%20prize%20money)

The [PGA Tour](https://progolfnow.com/golf-tours/pga/)returned to the iconic East Lake GC for the final event of the season, the 2025 Tour Championship in Atlanta, Georgia.

One year after the historic venue underwent significant changes ahead of last season's finale, the Tour Championship itself saw a revamped format ahead of the 2025 FedEx Cup decider with the removal of the staggered strokes system. The result ramped up the drama as anyone in the elite 30-man field had a legitimate chance at hoisting this year's FedEx Cup.

With two majors in hand this year and a FedEx Cup title to defend, world No.1 Scottie Scheffler came into the season finale as the clear favorite to repeat the feat. However, it's [Tommy Fleetwood](https://progolfnow.com/2025-tour-championship-tommy-fleetwood-cameron-young-went-low-east-lake-round-2) and Patrick Cantlay who sit atop the leaderboard heading into the final round and are threatening to claim the FedEx Cup crown for themselves.

Fleetwood, who took a share of the lead into Moving Day at the Tour Championship, would maintain his position after 54 holes after posting a solid 3-under 67 in round three of the season-ending event. Cantlay, the 2021 FedEx Cup champion, ensured that he would join Fleetwood at the top of the leaderboard going into the final round after a sublime 6-under 64 on Saturday at East Lake.

Whether it was Fleetwood, who would look to make his first PGA Tour win a FedEx Cup, Cantlay, who looked to win for the first time since the 2022 BMW Championship, Scheffler, or any of the chasing pack, whoever emerges victorious is guaranteed not only one of the Tour's most prestigious titles, but an extraoridnary winner's share from the season's biggest prize purse.

How much is on the line, though? Let's dive into the full breakdown of the prize money up for grabs at this year's Tour Championship.

Tour Championship purse 2025: Total purse and winner's prize money
------------------------------------------------------------------

The 2025 edition of the Tour Championship will feature the largest prize of the season, a humongous $40 million purse, with this year's FedEx Cup champion collecting a cool $10 million, 25% of the overall prize purse.

With the revamped Tour Championship format, the prize money available at East Lake has actually decreased from the whopping [$83 million](https://progolfnow.com/posts/tour-championship-payout-distribution-purse-prize-money-2024-01j6nenr3emj) that was divvied out at last season's finale. Additional prize money was awarded at the end of the Wyndham Championship and BMW Championship as part of the changes implemented in 2025.

Tour Championship payout distribution by finishing position in 2025
-------------------------------------------------------------------

In addition to the massive $10 million the champion at East Lake will collect, here is a look at the entire prize money breakdown by finishing position at the Tour Championship.

| **Finishing Position** | **Tour Championship Prize Money** |
| --- | --- |
| Winner | $10,000,000 |
| 2nd | $5,000,000 |
| 3rd | $3,705,000 |
| 4th | $3,200,000 |
| 5th | $2,750,000 |
| 6th | $1,900,000 |
| 7th | $1,400,000 |
| 8th | $1,065,000 |
| 9th | $900,000 |
| 10th | $735,000 |
| 11th | $695,000 |
| 12th | $660,000 |
| 13th | $625,000 |
| 14th | $590,000 |
| 15th | $560,000 |
| 16th | $505,000 |
| 17th | $490,000 |
| 18th | $475,000 |
| 19th | $460,000 |
| 20th | $445,000 |
| 21st | $430,000 |
| 22nd | $415,000 |
| 23rd | $400,000 |
| 24th | $390,000 |
| 25th | $380,000 |
| 26th | $375,000 |
| 27th | $370,000 |
| 28th | $365,000 |
| 29th | $360,000 |
| 30th | $355,000 |

As mentioned, the money divvied out at the Tour Championship leads the way this season when it comes to prize money, with the season finale ranking ahead of[](https://www.nbcsports.com/golf/news/the-players-championship-2025-prize-money-full-payout-from-the-25-million-purse) The Players Championship ($25 million) in second.

All of this is reflected in the payout distribution, with the top eight finishers at East Lake collecting seven-figure prizes for their efforts. Meanwhile, those who finish inside the top half of the field will clear $500k in prize money, while finishing 30th in the 30-man field will still net a player a cool $355,000.

December 17th, 2025

By Australian Golf Digest

**Strong views, sharp analysis and stories that sparked debate — these were the opinion pieces our readers engaged with most in 2025.**

[![Image 1: Cameron Smith posing outdoors, wearing a white golf hat and polo shirt, along with a red box on the right side of the image that reads No.1.](https://www.australiangolfdigest.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Top-Opinion-2025-1-1024x538.webp)](https://www.australiangolfdigest.com.au/opinion-why-the-recent-cam-smith-media-pile-on-is-over-the-top-and-needs-to-stop/)

Geez, we’re a forgetful bunch. It was only three years ago –almost to the week –that Australian sports fans and mainstream media were shouting from the rooftops, on breakfast television and on back pages that “our” Cameron Smith was a major winner and an Open champion at St Andrews.

**[READ MORE](https://www.australiangolfdigest.com.au/opinion-why-the-recent-cam-smith-media-pile-on-is-over-the-top-and-needs-to-stop/)**

Golf failed maths, but it’s not too late to correct the record.

Golf’s tee-marker debate refuses to go away

#### [This drastic re-imagining is the perfect solution to the PGA Tour’s FedEx Cup playoffs](https://www.australiangolfdigest.com.au/opinion-this-drastic-re-imagining-is-the-perfect-solution-to-the-pga-tours-fedex-cup-playoffs/)

The entire FedEx Cup playoffs should be overhauled, reduced in tournaments but increased in total players and re-imagined using a match play format with a twist – where top seeds compete in the first round to earn a bye or face a second chance saloon.

**[READ MORE](https://www.australiangolfdigest.com.au/opinion-this-drastic-re-imagining-is-the-perfect-solution-to-the-pga-tours-fedex-cup-playoffs/)**

[![Image 8: Scottie Scheffler, ranked number eight in the world, holds a golf trophy over his head as two men in suits behind him clap and a crowd looks on](https://www.australiangolfdigest.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Top-Opinion-2025-8-1024x538.webp)](https://www.australiangolfdigest.com.au/opinion-the-last-and-the-furious/)
#### [A list of out-of-the-box, and potentially laughable, suggestions to properly reward the most consistent golfer all PGA Tour season](https://www.australiangolfdigest.com.au/opinion-the-last-and-the-furious/)

Earlier this year, the PGA Tour announced it would eliminate the controversial starting-strokes format from this month’s season-ending Tour Championship. The 2024 edition marked the fifth year with the adjusted scoring system at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta. The FedEx Cup leader, Scottie Scheffler, started at 10-under-par (and eventually won), while second place teed off with an eight-under total and they all played 72 holes from there. But for this year’s Tour Championship from August 21-24, all 30 players in the field will start at even-par.

#### PGA Tour eliminates starting strokes from Tour Championship

![Image 7: Golfer wearing a white cap and light blue shirt is swinging a golf club](https://www.bssnews.net/assets/news_photos/2025/05/28/image-277449-1748402420.jpg)

MIAMI, May 28, 2025 (BSS/AFP) - Starting strokes will be eliminated from the season-ending Tour Championship, the PGA Tour announced on Tuesday, with the 30-man playoff finale being played as a 72-hole stroke-play tournament.

Players in past years had been given a staggered lead based on FedEx Cup season points, with last year's winner Scottie Scheffler starting at 10-under and finishing on 30-under to beat fellow American Collin Morikawa by four strokes after Morikawa began on four-under.

Over 72 holes, Morikawa was 26-under and Scheffler was 20-under but the starting strokes edge gave Scheffler the FedEx Cup playoff crown.

The tour's player advisory council and policy board approved changes to the playoff format on Tuesday that will have all players starting at level par as in a usual tournament.

The new format will be played in this year's Tour Championship at East Lake Golf Club in Atlanta from August 21 to 24.

"Today's announcement is an important first step in the evolution of our post-season," said PGA Tour commissioner Jay Monahan.

"The Player Advisory Council led a thorough process to respond to what our fans are asking for: The most competitive golf in the world, played for the highest stakes, in the most straightforward and engaging format."

Other changes to the Tour Championship include changing course set-ups to encourage more risk-reward choices throughout each round to help build drama.

The playoff format will narrow the field to 30 golfers but the player advisory council is studying the qualification system with an eye to boosting the value of season points and keeping the field the toughest to reach on tour.

Other ideas are being considered with possible announcements coming later this year.

"We want the Tour Championship to be the hardest tournament to qualify for and the FedEx Cup trophy the most difficult to win," world number one Scheffler said.

"Shifting the Tour Championship to a more straight-up format with a tougher course set-up makes it easier for fans to follow and provides a more challenging test for players -- which brings out the best competition."

This year's Tour Championship will feature the top 30 players in points who have advanced from two prior playoff events: the 70-player St. Jude Championship at TPC Southwind in Memphis and the 50-player BMW Championship at Caves Valley Golf Club in Owings Mills, Maryland.

Tommy Fleetwood was named FedEx Cup champion for his maiden PGA Tour victory at the [East Lake](https://www.golfmonthly.com/travel/usa/how-can-i-play-east-lake-golf-club) event, banking a huge $10m one-off payment for his achievement

[](https://www.golfmonthly.com/news/fedex-cup-playoffs-2025-prize-money-payout)
However, that was far from the only money available throughout August’s three Playoffs, with plenty of bonus payments up for grabs as well as tournament prize money.

 You may like 
*   [![Image 27: Tommy Fleetwood acknowledges fans ](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/RMzH3qQ4D7ZDP8bdae7QkP-1280-80.jpg)How Much Money Tommy Fleetwood Has Won In 2025](https://www.golfmonthly.com/news/how-much-tommy-fleetwood-earned-won-2025)
*   [![Image 28: (L to R) Marco Penge, Rory McIlroy holds up the Race To Dubai trophy in 2025, Matt Fitzpatrick](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/KW6DqA3VxpXUw6SezgnDPL-1280-80.jpg)Race To Dubai Bonus Pool Payout 2025](https://www.golfmonthly.com/news/race-to-dubai-bonus-payout-breakdown-2025)
*   [![Image 29: Matt Fitzpatrick with the DP World Tour Championship trophy ](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/GqFqzZ9cKGoWQzLSBBaCFF-1280-80.jpg)How Much Did Matt Fitzpatrick Win At The DP World Tour Championship?](https://www.golfmonthly.com/news/dp-world-tour-championship-prize-money-payout-2025)

The first $20m in bonus money was handed out to the top 10 in the FedEx Cup standings after the Wyndham Championship, with Scottie Scheffler claiming half of that figure for his position at the top of the standings at that point.

The first of the Playoffs, the FedEx St. Jude Championship, then distributed $20m in prize money, with each player in the field earning a share and winner Justin Rose claiming the top prize of $3.6m.

Another $20m was handed out among the 50 who made it through to the second of the Playoffs, [the BMW Championship](https://www.golfmonthly.com/news/bmw-championship-prize-money-payout-2025).

Scheffler again cashed in that week, first with his $3.6m in prize money for his victory and also thanks to the second wave of FedEx Cup bonus money.

That came to a total of $22.93m distributed among the top 30 in the FedEx Cup standings at the end of the tournament. Scheffler still led the way at that point, banking him another $5m.

![Image 30: Scottie Scheffler at the BMW Championship](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vThfqWLtzajnyeTwmHX49i.jpg)

Scottie Scheffler won over $22m in the FedEx Cup Playoffs

(Image credit: Getty Images)

The top 30 in the FedEx Cup standings then took their places in the field for the Tour Championship, where another $40m was distributed among the competitors.

Even then, the payouts weren't complete, with an additional $17.08m in deferrals to be divided among players ranked 31st-150th in the FedEx Cup standings.

*   [![Image 31: Tommy Fleetwood acknowledges fans ](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/RMzH3qQ4D7ZDP8bdae7QkP-1280-80.jpg)How Much Money Tommy Fleetwood Has Won In 2025](https://www.golfmonthly.com/news/how-much-tommy-fleetwood-earned-won-2025)
*   [![Image 32: (L to R) Marco Penge, Rory McIlroy holds up the Race To Dubai trophy in 2025, Matt Fitzpatrick](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/KW6DqA3VxpXUw6SezgnDPL-1280-80.jpg)Race To Dubai Bonus Pool Payout 2025](https://www.golfmonthly.com/news/race-to-dubai-bonus-payout-breakdown-2025)
*   [![Image 33: Matt Fitzpatrick with the DP World Tour Championship trophy ](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/GqFqzZ9cKGoWQzLSBBaCFF-1280-80.jpg)How Much Did Matt Fitzpatrick Win At The DP World Tour Championship?](https://www.golfmonthly.com/news/dp-world-tour-championship-prize-money-payout-2025)

The figures in the table below include those deferred payments for the players who ranked 31st-70th in the FedEx Cup standings and therefore competed in the Playoffs, with a range between $250,000 for the player in 31st and $175,000 for the player in 70th.

Players who finished between 71st and 150th earn deferrals ranging between $140,000 and $85,000, bringing the combined FedEx Cup bonus money to $100m.

As the table shows, despite not being named FedEx Cup champion, thanks largely to his bonus money, Scheffler made the most money of anyone in the Playoffs, with $22,376,667.

Second on the list is Fleetwood on $14,070,000, with Rory McIlroy in third on $8,336,000, despite [skipping the first of the Playoffs, the FedEx St. Jude Championship](https://www.golfmonthly.com/news/why-is-rory-mcilroy-skipping-the-fedex-st-jude-championship). Check out the full list here.

===============

EAST LAKE GOLF CLUB
-------------------

East Lake Golf Club is a private facility located approximately five miles east of downtown Atlanta. Established in 1904, East Lake was the home course of the legendary golfer Bobby Jones and much of its Clubhouse serves as a tribute to his accomplishments. Over the years, the golf course has hosted many golf tournaments including the 1950 U.S. Women's Amateur, 1963 Ryder Cup, and 2001 U.S. Men's Amateur. It is now the permanent home of the TOUR Championship, the culminating event of the FedExCup Playoffs. Proceeds from operations, as well as charitable donations from the club’s corporate membership, support the East Lake Foundation and its remarkable redevelopment project.

**[ABOUT THE CLUB](https://www.eastlakegolfclub.com/)**

THE RESTORATION
---------------

It’s a new era for historic East Lake Golf Club.  
  
Using previously unknown aerial photography from 1949, architect Andrew Green has finalized a complete restoration of the course, combining elements of the original vision with exciting new changes that reflect the modern game and provide a worthy test for players of every level, including the PGA TOUR’s very best during the TOUR Championship.  
  
A crowning achievement for East Lake, this transformation will serve as a model for golf courses around the country looking to reimagine championship golf as a platform for progress.

7.content:
**ATLANTA —** The field is set for the 2025 TOUR Championship with the top 30 players in the FedExCup qualifying for the season finale at East Lake Golf Club. Reigning FedExCup Champion Scottie Scheffler earned his 18th win of his PGA TOUR career and his fifth victory of the 2025 season at the BMW Championship, maintaining his place as the FedExCup leader for the fourth consecutive season as he seeks to become the first back-to-back FedExCup Champion.

Rory McIlroy, who won the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am, THE PLAYERS Championship and the Masters Tournament this season, collected a T12 finish at Caves Valley Golf Club and will enter the week at No. 2 in the FedExCup. J.J. Spaun, who earned his second TOUR title in dramatic fashion at the U.S. Open at Oakmont, enters at No. 3 while 2018 FedExCup Champion Justin Rose sits at No. 4 following his victory at the first Playoffs event, the FedEx St. Jude Championship. Tommy Fleetwood finished T4 at the BMW Championship and rounds out the top five in the standings.

The FedExCup Playoffs conclude this week at the TOUR Championship, supported by Proud Partners Accenture, Coca-Cola and Southern Company, where the top 30 players will compete for the title of 2025 FedExCup Champion. The first and second rounds will be broadcast live on Golf Channel from historic East Lake Golf Club on Thursday, Aug. 21 and Friday, Aug. 22 from 1-6 p.m. The third round will be broadcast on Golf Channel from 1-2:30 p.m. and on NBC from 2:30-7 p.m. on Saturday, Aug. 23, with the final round slated for Sunday, Aug. 24 from 12-1:30 p.m. on Golf Channel and 1:30-6 p.m. on NBC.

As previously announced, the TOUR Championship will be played as a 72-hole stroke-play event, with all players starting the tournament at even par and the winner claiming the FedExCup.

Other Player Storylines:
------------------------

*   Reigning FedExCup Champion Scottie Scheffler (No. 1) holds the FedExCup lead entering the TOUR Championship for the fourth consecutive year (T2/2022; T6/2023; 1st/2024). Scheffler looks to become the first back-to-back FedExCup Champion.
*   Harry Hall (No. 45 to No. 26) was the only player to begin the BMW Championship outside the top 30 in the FedExCup and play his way into the TOUR Championship following his sixth-place finish at Caves Valley.
*   Seven players are making their TOUR Championship debut:
    *   J.J. Spaun (No. 3)
    *   Ben Griffin (No. 6)
    *   Maverick McNealy (No. 10)
    *   Andrew Novak (No. 15)
    *   Harry Hall (No. 26)
    *   Jacob Bridgeman (No. 27)
    *   Chris Gotterup (No. 29)
*   Six former FedExCup Champions qualified for the TOUR Championship: No. 1 Scottie Scheffler (2024), No. 2 Rory McIlroy (2016, 2019, 2022), No. 4 Justin Rose (2018), No. 12 Justin Thomas (2017), No. 20 Patrick Cantlay (2021), No. 22 Viktor Hovland (2023).
*   Rory McIlroy qualified for his eighth consecutive TOUR Championship, the longest active streak. Tony Finau and Xander Schauffele entered the Playoffs sharing the longest active streak (8) before failing to advance past the FedEx St. Jude Championship and BMW Championship, respectively.
